claims.text: Computational methods can be used to design ceramic or powder materials with modified particle size distributions.
Modifying the particle size distribution can reduce the required sintering temperature.
Optimizing particle size distribution reduces the activation energy required for sintering.
Reducing the activation energy required for sintering enables sintering at a lower temperature.
The proposed intervention will reduce the sintering temperature by at least 100°C relative to conventional processing.
The proposed material can be sintered below 800°C.
The magnitude of the sintering-temperature reduction depends on the specific material and computational method.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires a reduction of at least 100°C, but the hypothesis is declared falsified only for reductions below 50°C. Results from 50°C up to less than 100°C would violate the quantitative prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
